analysis:
The change is confined to scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py, a CI test harness for the Darkbloom runner-routing step. It does not touch provider, coordinator, attestation, encryption, cache or key-handling code, so no threat-model asset (A-001..A-020) or provider trust boundary (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-011..TB-014) is affected at runtime.

I read the head text (lines 1-993 plus the base tail) and the patch hunks. New behavior in the head version:
- Adds a DISPATCH count expression and a desktop.yml `desktop-package` macOS routed lane.
- Resizes PLAN_LANES, adds GPU shard lanes, and adds UNSIZED_PLAN_REQUEST and BLOCKING_TESTS.
- Adds a Linux `watchdog` and an `hourly` workflow check.
- Adds a test that only dispatched runs report failures, with `issues: write` limited to the ci-dev `hourly-failures` job.

The tests strengthen existing controls on CI routing:
- Routed jobs must have read-only permissions, no id-token, no secrets and bounded timeouts.
- Release and credentialed workflows (UNROUTED) keep literal blacksmith runners and never carry self-hosted or darkbloom labels.
- Fork pull requests never contact the plane.
- Only an exact label array is accepted from the plane.
- The plane URL must be https and certificate verification stays on.
- Plane text cannot inject workflow commands or markdown.

The visible diff weakens none of these assertions. The one pre-existing loosening visible is that `required` lane handling is no longer used in PLAN_LANES; this is a CI cost/routing detail, not a security control.

The patch excerpt is truncated and the workflow YAML files are not supplied. Whether the actual workflows (desktop.yml, darkbloom-watchdog.yml, ci-dev-hourly.yml) satisfy these assertions is not verifiable here. The tests would fail in CI if they did not.

No findings.
